# Identifying the impacts of extreme weather

The output for this assignment should include:

- Comparision map of night light intensities before and after the storm
- A map of the homes in Houston that lost power
- Find the estimate number of homes in Houston that lost power
- Write a brief reflection (approx. 100 words) summarizing your results and discussing any limitations to this study

## Backgrgound

In February 2021, there was a devastating power outage that affected the state of Texas due to several storms that plunged the state into freezing temperatures. Texas runs on independent energy, so once a power outage occurs, it is almost impossible to secure energy from neighboring states which is unique to their governing infrastructures. From the storms, hundreds of deaths occurred.


### Load and prep data

```{r}
# Load libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(sf) # Simple features for spatial vector
library(here)
library(terra)
library(stars) # Raster
library(tmap)
library(kableExtra)
```

```{r}
# Load night lights data from VIIRS 
viirs_feb_7a <- rast(here(
  "data", "VNP46A1", "VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v05.001.2021039064328.tif"))

viirs_feb_7b <- rast(here(
  "data", "VNP46A1", "VNP46A1.A2021038.h08v06.001.2021039064329.tif"))

viirs_feb_16a <- rast(here(
  "data", "VNP46A1", "VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v05.001.2021048091106.tif"))

viirs_feb_16b <- rast(here(
  "data", "VNP46A1", "VNP46A1.A2021047.h08v06.001.2021048091105.tif"))
```

```{r, results = 'hide'}
# Load roads data using st_read and the query insert given as tip
roads <- st_read(here(
  "data", "gis_osm_roads_free_1.gpkg"), 
  query = "SELECT * FROM gis_osm_roads_free_1 WHERE fclass='motorway'")


# load buildings using st_read and the query insert given as tip
buildings <- st_read(here(
  "data", "gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1.gpkg"),
   query = "SELECT *
    FROM gis_osm_buildings_a_free_1
    WHERE (type IS NULL AND name IS NULL)
    OR type in ('residential', 'apartments', 'house', 'static_caravan', 'detached')")

```

```{r}
# Bounding box information given for Houston
houston <- st_bbox(
  c(xmin = -96.5, ymin = 29.0, xmax = -94.5, ymax = 30.5),
  crs = st_crs(4326))
```

```{r}
# test if roads and buildings CRS matches 
if(st_crs(roads) == st_crs(buildings)) {
  print("coordinate reference systems match")}
```

```{r}
# mergen the data to respective date
viirs_feb_7 <- merge(viirs_feb_7a, viirs_feb_7b) 
viirs_feb_16 <- merge(viirs_feb_16a, viirs_feb_16b)
```

```{r}
# test viirs CRS
if(st_crs(viirs_feb_7 ) == st_crs(viirs_feb_16)) {
  print("coordinate reference systems match")}
```

### Before and After

```{r}
before <- crop(viirs_feb_7, houston)
```
```{r}
after <- crop(viirs_feb_16, houston)
```

```{r}
# Masking values below zero and capping at 800 (perhaps higher this)
mask_before <- before
mask_before[(mask_before>1000 | (mask_before <=0))] <- NA

mask_after <- after
mask_after[(mask_after>1000 | (mask_after <=0))] <- NA
```

```{r}
# Combine the two for mapping comparisions
before_after <- c(mask_before, mask_after)
```

```{r}
# Rename layers

names(before_after) <- c("February 7, 2021", "February 16, 2021")
```


```{r}
# Map before storm
tm_shape(before_after) +
    tm_raster(
    col.scale = tm_scale_continuous(values = 'magma'),
    col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Light Intensity nW (cm^2 sr^1)")
    ) +
    tm_title("Houston night lights before and after storm (February 2021)") +
    tm_facets(ncol = 2,
    free.scales = FALSE) +
    tm_graticules(lwd = 0.4,
    col = "whitesmoke",
    alpha = 0.5,
    n.x= 5,
    n.y = 5)
    

col.legend = tm_legend(title = "Light Intensity nW (cm^2 sr^1)", size = 1.2)
```

### Create blackout mask

```{r}
# Find the change in night lights intensity
change <- viirs_feb_7 - viirs_feb_16
```

```{r}
# Reclassify change
rcl_change <-  matrix(c(
    -Inf, 200, NA,
    200, Inf, 1), nco = 3, byrow = TRUE)

mask_change <- classify(change, rcl = rcl_change)
```

```{r}
# Vectorize blackout mask
black_out <- as.polygons(mask_change) |> 
    st_as_sf() |> 
    st_make_valid()
```

```{r}
# Crop to match the extent of Houston
black_out_houston <- st_crop(black_out, houston)
```

```{r}
# Reproject to 3083 
blackout <- st_transform(black_out_houston, crs = 3083)
```


### Exclude highways from the cropped blackout mask

```{r}
# test if roads CRS if not then matche blackout
if(st_crs(roads) == st_crs(blackout)) {
  print("coordinate reference systems match")
  } else{
  new_roads <- st_transform(roads, crs = st_crs(blackout))
}
```

```{r}
# test if houston CRS if not then matche blackout
if(st_crs(houston) == st_crs(blackout)) {
  print("coordinate reference systems match")
  } else{
  new_houston <- st_transform(houston, crs = st_crs(blackout))
}
```

```{r}
# union
roads_union <- st_union(new_roads)
```

```{r}
# Create buffer zone
roads_buffer <- st_buffer(roads_union, dist = 200)
```

```{r}
# 
blackout_difference_roads <- st_difference(blackout, roads_buffer)
```


### Identify the number of homes likely impacted by blackouts

```{r}
# 
building <- st_transform(buildings, crs = 3083)
```

```{r}
# 
blackout_buildings <- building |> 
    st_filter(blackout_difference_roads)
```

```{r}
# Find the number of houses blackout
n_houses <- nrow(blackout_buildings)
```

```{r}
# Table for number of houses
n_houses |> 
  kable(caption = "Houses impacted by Texas power outage (Feb. 2021)" ,
  col.names = c("# Impacted Houses")) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"))
```

```{r}
# Map houses that were affected by blackout

tm_basemap("OpenStreetMap") +
    tm_shape(blackout_difference_roads) + # houses
    tm_shape(blackout_buildings) +
    tm_polygons() +
    tm_scalebar() +
    tm_compass(type = "rose", position = c("left", "top"), size = 1.5) +
    tm_title("Estimed houses impacted by power outage") +
    tm_add_legend(
      type = "polygons",
      labels = "Power Outage",
      fill = "darkgrey"
    )
    
```

### Reflection 

The number of homes that were impacted was found to be 157,408 in Houston during the power outage in February 2021 that was caused by extreme storm conditions. One limitation to this particular study is not knowing the exact extent to who was impacted and potentially being excluded. This is important for developing recovery plans surrounding those heavily affected and may have lost income from loss of work or even experiencing personal loss. During the data manipulation, we created a buffer to exclude roads, but this may also exclude homes if they overlapped, which may have occurred during `st_difference`. Overall, more exploration on this matter must be conducted to give a fair and adequate research to provide an equitable solution for future scenarios in case of severe winter storms.
